questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = x\cos^{- 1} ⁡ \left(- sin ⁡ \left|x\right|\right), x \in \left[- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right],$ then which of the following is true?
options: $f'$ is increasing in $\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)$ and decreasing in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
$f'$ is decreasing in $\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)$ and increasing in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = x\left(\pi - \cos^{- 1}\left(sin\left|x\right|\right)\right) = x ( \pi\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{- 1}\left(sin\left|x\right|\right)\right) = x\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \left|x\right|\right)$
$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}x\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + x\right) & x \ge 0 \\ x\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) & x < 0\end{cases}\right$
${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2x & x \ge 0 \\ \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2x & x < 0\end{cases}\right$
${f}^{'}\left(x\right)$ is increasing in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and decreasing in $\left(\dfrac{- \pi}{2}, 0\right)$.

questions.q: The number of real roots of the equation ${e}^{4x} + 2{e}^{3x} - {e}^{x} - 6 = 0$ is :
questions.solution:
Given that

${e}^{4x} + 2{e}^{3x} - {e}^{x} - 6 = 0$

Let ${e}^{x} = t$, $t > 0$

$f ( t ) = {t}^{4} + 2{t}^{3} - t - 6$
$f ' ( t ) = 4{t}^{3} + 6{t}^{2} - 1$

${f}^{' '} ( t ) = 12{t}^{2} + 12t > 0$ $( t > 0 )$

$f ' ( t )$ is increasing function

Now ${f}^{'} ( 0 ) = - 1$

${f}^{'} ( 1 ) = 9$

By using Intermediate value theorem there exists a root for $f\left(x\right) = 0$if $f\left(\alpha\right)f\left(\beta\right) < 0 ⇒ f\left(\gamma\right) = 0, \gamma \in \left(\alpha, \beta\right)$

So ${f}^{'} ( \beta ) = 0$

Hence, only one real root.

questions.q: For the function $f\left(x\right) = 4{\log}_{e}\left(x - 1\right) - 2{x}^{2} + 4x + 5, x > 1$, which one of the following is NOT correct?
options: $f\left(x\right)$ is increasing in $\left(1, 2\right)$  and decreasing in $\left(2, \infty\right)$
$f\left(x\right) = 0$ has a root in the interval $\left(e, e + 1\right)$
questions.solution:
Given $f\left(x\right) = 4{\log}_{e}\left(x - 1\right) - 2{x}^{2} + 4x + 5, x > 1$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4}{x - 1} - 4\left(x - 1\right)$

For $1 0$

For $x > 2 ⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) < 0$

Hence, $f\left(x\right)$ has a maxima at $x = 2$

$f\left(x\right) = - 1$ has two solution as the curve of $f\left(x\right)$ will cut it at exactly two points.

Now, $f\left(e\right) > 0$ and $f\left(e + 1\right) < 0$

i.e. $f\left(e\right) \cdot f\left(e + 1\right) < 0$

${f}^{'}\left(e\right) - {f}^{"}\left(2\right) = \dfrac{4}{e - 1} - 4\left(e - 1\right) + 8 > 0$

questions.q: A box open from top is made from a rectangular sheet of dimension $a \times b$ by cutting squares each of side $x$ from each of the four corners and folding up the flaps. If the volume of the box is maximum, then $x$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given that: A box open from top is made from a rectangular sheet dimension $a \times b$ by cutting squares each of side $x$ from each of the four corners and folding up the flaps and the volume of the box is maximum.

dimensions of the box:

$L = a - 2x, B = b - 2x \text{ and } H = x$

$V = L \times B \times H$

$V ( x ) = ( a - 2x ) ( b - 2x ) x$

$V ( x ) = 4{x}^{3} - 2 ( a + b ) {x}^{2} + abx$

For volume to be maximum:
${V}^{'} ( x ) = 12{x}^{2} - 4 ( a + b ) x + ab = 0$

$x = \dfrac{4 ( a + b ) - \sqrt{16{a}^{2} + 16{b}^{2} - 16ab}}{24}$$\left[+ cannotbetakenasx < a, b\right]$,
for maximum volume, $x = \dfrac{a + b - \sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} - ab}}{6}$

For $\dfrac{1}{2} 0$

Hence, $f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + f\left(1\right) = 3 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 + 2cos1\right)sin1$

questions.q: The number of distinct real roots of the equation ${x}^{7} - 7x - 2 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

${x}^{7} - 7x - 2 = 0$

${x}^{7} - 7x = 2$

Now taking $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{7} - 7x$ (odd) & $y = 2$

Now differentiating $f\left(x\right)$ w.r.t $x$ we get,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 7\left({x}^{6} - 1\right) = 7\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)\left({x}^{4} + {x}^{2} + 1\right)$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0 ⇒ x = \pm 1$

So points of extrema are $- 1 \text{ and } 1$, Now plotting the graph to check number of solution we get,

$f\left(x\right) = 2$ has $3$ real distinct solution.

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ and $g: R \to R$ be two functions defined by $f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) - {e}^{- x} + 1$ and $g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1 - 2{e}^{2x}}{{e}^{x}} \cdot$ Then, for which of the following range of $\alpha$, the inequality $f\left(g\left(\dfrac{{\left(\alpha - 1\right)}^{2}}{3}\right)\right) > f\left(g\left(\alpha - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\right)$ holds?
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) - {e}^{- x} + 1 ⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2x}{{x}^{2} + 1} + {e}^{- x} > 0, ∀ x \in R$

So $f\left(x\right)$ increasing

$g\left(x\right) = {e}^{- x} - 2{e}^{x} ⇒ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = - \left({e}^{- x} + 2{e}^{x}\right) < 0 ∀ x \in R$

So $g\left(x\right)$ decreasing

$⇒ f\left(g\left(x\right)\right)$ is decreasing

$⇒ f\left(g\left(\dfrac{( \alpha - 1{)}^{2}}{3}\right)\right) > f\left(g\left(\alpha - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(\alpha - 1\right)}^{2}}{3} < \alpha - \dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ \left(\alpha - 2\right)\left(\alpha - 3\right) < 0 ⇒ \alpha \in \left(2, 3\right)$

From options

questions.q: A wire of length $22m$ is to be cut into two pieces. One of the pieces is to be made into a square and the other into an equilateral triangle. Then, the length of the side of the equilateral triangle, so that the combined area of the square and the equilateral triangle is minimum, is
questions.solution:
Let the side of square be $\dfrac{22 - l}{4}$ and side of triangle be $\dfrac{l}{3}$ ,

So, total area is given by $\Delta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}{\left(\dfrac{l}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{22 - l}{4}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ \Delta = \dfrac{1}{12\sqrt{3}} \cdot {l}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{16}{\left(22 - l\right)}^{2}$

Differentiating with respect to $l$ to get maxima and minima points,

$⇒ \dfrac{d\Delta}{dl} = \dfrac{1}{6\sqrt{3}} \cdot l - \dfrac{1}{8}\left(22 - l\right) = 0$ $⇒ l = \dfrac{66\sqrt{3}}{4 + 3\sqrt{3}}$

Also$\dfrac{{d}^{2}\Delta}{d{l}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{6\sqrt{3}} + \dfrac{1}{8}$ ($+ ve$. which is case of minima)

So, side of triangle will be $= \dfrac{l}{3} = \dfrac{22\sqrt{3}}{4 + 3\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{66}{4\sqrt{3} + 9}$

questions.q: The sum of the abosolute maximum and minimum values of the function $f\left(x\right) = \left|{x}^{2} - 5x + 6\right| - 3x + 2$ in the interval $\left[- 1, 3\right]$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left|{x}^{2} - 5x + 6\right| - 3x + 2$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left|\left(x - 3\right)\left(x - 2\right)\right| - 3x + 2$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{x}^{2} - 8x + 8 & ; x \in \left[- 1, 2\right] \\ - {x}^{2} + 2x - 4 & ; x \in ( 2, 3 ]\end{cases}\right$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}2x - 8 & ; x \in \left(- 1, 2\right) \\ - x + 2 & ; x \in \left(2, 3\right)\end{cases}\right$

Now point of extrema will be $2x - 8 = 0 ⇒ x = 4$which is not in domain and $- x + 2 = 0 ⇒ x = 2$

Now for finding the value of global minima and maxima we will check the value of function at extrema points and boundary points,

So, $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} - 8x + 8$ will give, $f\left(- 1\right) = 17 \text{ and } f\left(2\right) = - 4$

And $f\left(x\right) = - {x}^{2} + 2x - 4$ will give, $f\left(2\right) = 4, f\left(3\right) = - 7$

Hence, absolute minima is $- 7$ and maxima is $17$

So, their sum is $- 7 + 17 = 10$

questions.q:
Let $f: \left[2, 4\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $\left(x{\log}_{e}x\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left({\log}_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) \ge 1, x \in \left[2, 4\right]$ with $f\left(2\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $f\left(4\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.
Consider the following two statements:

(A) $f\left(x\right) \le 1, \text{for all}x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

(B) $f\left(x\right) \ge 1 / 8, \text{for all}x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

Then,
options: Neither statement $( A )$ nor statement $( B )$ is true
Both the statements $( A )$and $( B )$are true
questions.solution:
Given,

Domain and range of function,

$f: \left[2, 4\right] \to \mathbb{R}$

$\left(x{\log}_{e}x\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left({\log}_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) \ge 1, x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

$⇒ \left(x{\log}_{e}x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}f\left(x\right) + \left({\log}_{e}x\right)f\left(x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\right) + xf\left(x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({\log}_{e}x\right) \ge 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left[xlnxf\left(x\right)\right] \ge 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left[xlnxf\left(x\right)\right] \ge \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left[xlnxf\left(x\right) - x\right] \ge 0$

Hence, $h ( x ) = x\left(lnx\right)f\left(x\right) - x$ is a increasing function,

$∴ h ( x ) \ge h ( 2 ) , x \in [ 2, 4 ]$

$⇒ xlnx \times f\left(x\right) - x \ge 2ln2 \times f\left(2\right) - 2$

$⇒ xlnxf ( x ) - x \ge ln2 - 2$

Similarly, $h\left(x\right) \le h\left(4\right)$

$⇒ xlnxf\left(x\right) - x \le ln4 - 4$

So, $\dfrac{ln2 - 2}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \le f ( x ) \le \dfrac{ln4 - 4}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx}$

Now for $x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

$\dfrac{ln4 - 4}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \le \dfrac{ln4 - 4}{2ln2} + \dfrac{1}{ln2} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{ln2} < 1$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) \le 1\text{for}x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

Now for $x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

$\dfrac{ln2 - 2}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \ge \dfrac{ln2 - 2}{4ln4} + \dfrac{1}{ln4} = \dfrac{ln2 - 2}{4ln4} + \dfrac{1}{ln4} = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4ln2} > \dfrac{1}{8}$

Hence, $f ( x ) \ge \dfrac{1}{8}$

Hence both $A$ & $B$ are correct.
Note this question was bonus in Jee Main 2023 April session, as LMVT on $f ( x ) \cdot xlnx$ can't be satisfied.

Hence, no such $f ( x )$ exist.

questions.q: The absolute minimum value, of the function $f\left(x\right) = \left|{x}^{2} - x + 1\right| + \left[{x}^{2} - x + 1\right]$, where $\left[t\right]$ denotes the greatest integer function, in the interval $\left[- 1, 2\right]$, is
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = \left[{x}^{2} - x + 1\right] + \left|{x}^{2} - x + 1\right|x \in \left[- 1, 2\right]$

$∵ \left|{x}^{2} - x + 1\right| \to \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right) > 0$

$∴ f\left(x\right) = \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right) + \left[{x}^{2} - x + 1\right]$

Now,

Consider $g ( x ) = \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right)$

For the minimum value of $g ( x )$,

$g ' ( x ) = 0 ⇒ 2x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right)$ attains its minimum value at $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

And $\text{min}\left[{x}^{2} - x + 1\right] = 0\text{as}{x}^{2} - x + 1 > 0$

$⇒ f\left(x\right)$ attains its minimum at $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So, $f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4} + 0 = \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: The set of all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ for which the equation $x | x - 1 | + | x + 2 | + a = 0$ has exactly one real root, is
questions.solution:
Given,

$x | x - 1 | + | x + 2 | + a = 0$

Now taking, Case I: $x < - 2$, we get

$- {x}^{2} + x - x - 2 + a = 0$

$⇒ a = {x}^{2} + 2$

And $y = {x}^{2} + 2$ is decreasing $∀ x \in ( - \infty , - 2 )$

Now taking Case II: $- 2 \le x < 1$ we get,

$- {x}^{2} + x + x + 2 + a = 0$

$⇒ a = {x}^{2} - 2x - 2$

And $y = {x}^{2} - 2x - 2$

So, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 1 \le 0 ∀ x \in [ - 2, 1 )$

Hence, $y$ is decreasing $∀ x \in [ - 2, 1 )$

Now taking Case III: $x \ge 1$ we get,

${x}^{2} - x + x + 2 + a = 0$

$⇒ a = - \left({x}^{2} + 2\right)$

And $y = - \left({x}^{2} + 2\right)$ is decreasing $∀ x \in [ 1, \infty )$

Hence, from all the cases we can say that nature of function is continuously decreasing so, it will cut $x -$axis only one time,

$∴$ Exactly one real root $∀ a \in R$

questions.solution:

${f}^{"}\left(x\right) = {g}^{"}\left(x\right) + 6x \ldots \left(1\right)$

${f}^{'}\left(1\right) = 4{g}^{'}\left(1\right) - 3 = 9 \ldots \left(2\right)$

$f\left(2\right) = 3g\left(2\right) = 12 \ldots \left(3\right)$

By integrating $\left(1\right)$, we get
${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {g}^{'}\left(x\right) + 3{x}^{2} + C$

At $x = 1$

${f}^{'}\left(1\right) = {g}^{'}\left(1\right) + 3 + C$

$⇒ 9 = 3 + 3 + C ⇒ C = 3$

$∴ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {g}^{'}\left(x\right) + 3{x}^{2} + 3$

Again by integrating, we get

$f\left(x\right) = g\left(x\right) + {x}^{3} + 3x + D$

At $x = 2$, we get

$f\left(2\right) = g\left(2\right) + 8 + 3\left(2\right) + D$

$⇒ 12 = 4 + 8 + 6 + D ⇒ D = - 6$

So,

$f\left(x\right) = g\left(x\right) + {x}^{3} + 3x - 6$

Option $\left(A\right)$:

At $x = - 2$,

$⇒ g\left(- 2\right) - f\left(- 2\right) = 20$

So, this option is true.

Option $\left(B\right)$

If $- 1 < x < 2$

Let $h\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) - g\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} + 3x - 6$

$⇒ {h}^{'}\left(x\right) = 3{x}^{2} + 3$

$⇒ h ' \left(x\right) > 0$ for all values of $x$.

So, $h\left(- 1\right) < h\left(x\right) < h\left(2\right)$

$⇒ - 10 < h\left(x\right) < 8$

$⇒ \left|h\left(x\right)\right| < 10$

So, this option is NOT true.

Option $\left(C\right)$

${h}^{'}\left(x\right) = {f}^{'}\left(x\right) - {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = 3{x}^{2} + 3$

If $\left|{h}^{'}\left(x\right)\right| < 6 ⇒ \left|3{x}^{2} + 3\right| < 6$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2} + 3 < 6$ and $- 6 < 3{x}^{2} + 3$

$⇒ {x}^{2} < 1$ and ${x}^{2} > - 3\left(alwaystrue\right)$

$⇒ - 1 < x < 1$

So, If $x \in \left(- 1, 1\right)$ then $\left|{f}^{'}\left(x\right) - {g}^{'}\left(x\right)\right| < 6$

So, this option is true.

Option $\left(D\right)$

$f\left(x\right) - g\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{3} + 3x - 6 = 0$

$h\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} + 3x - 6$

Here, $h\left(1\right) = - ve$ and $h\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = + ve$

So, there exists ${x}_{0} \in \left(1, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ such that $f\left({x}_{0}\right) = g\left({x}_{0}\right)$

So, this option is true.

questions.q: If the integral ${∫}_{0}^{10}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x - \left[x\right]}}dx = \alpha{e}^{- 1} + \beta{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \gamma,$ where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are integers and $\left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x,$ then the value of $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{10}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x - \left[x\right]}}dx = {∫}_{0}^{10}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{\left\{x\right\}}}dx,$ where $x - \left[x\right] = \left\{x\right\}$ is the fractional part function.

We know that the $\left\{x\right\}$ is a periodic function with period $1$ and also that $sin2\pix$ is a periodic function with period $\dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi} = 1 .$

Thus, the function $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{\left\{x\right\}}}$ is periodic with period $1 .$

If $f\left(x\right)$ is a periodic function with period $T$ then ${∫}_{0}^{nT}f\left(x\right)dx = n{∫}_{0}^{T}f\left(x\right)dx, n \in N$

Therefore $I = 10{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{\left\{x\right\}}}dx$

$⇒ I = 10{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x}}dx$

Now, for $0 \le x \le 1 ⇒ - 1 \le sin2\pi x \le 1,$ hence $\left[sin2x\right]$ can take values $0$ and $- 1$

$⇒ I = 10\left({∫}_{0}^{1 / 2}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x}}dx + {∫}_{1 / 2}^{1}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x}}dx\right)$

$⇒ I = 10\left(0 + {∫}_{1 / 2}^{1}\dfrac{( - 1 )}{{e}^{x}}dx\right)$

$⇒ I = - 10{∫}_{1 / 2}^{1}{e}^{- x}dx$

$⇒ I = 10{\left[{e}^{- x}\right]}_{1 / 2}^{1}$

$⇒ I = 10\left({e}^{- 1} - {e}^{- 1 / 2}\right)$

Given, $I = \alpha{e}^{- 1} + \beta{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \gamma,$ thus $\alpha = 10, \beta = - 10, \gamma = 0 .$

And, $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 10 - 10 = 0 .$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\tan^{3}x \cdot \sin^{2}3x\left(2{sec}^{2}x \cdot \sin^{2}3x + 3tanx \cdot sin6x\right)dx$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Rearranging, we get,

${∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^{4}x\right)}{2} \cdot \sin^{4}3x + \tan^{4}x \cdot \dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\sin^{4}3x\right)}{2}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\left(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^{4}x \cdot \sin^{4}3x\right)\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[\tan^{4}x \cdot \sin^{4}3x\right]}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)}^{4} \times 0 - {\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)}^{4} \times 1\right]$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{9} = - \dfrac{1}{18}$

questions.q: If $\left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer $\le x,$ then ${\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}\left(sin\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){x}^{0}dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - 1\right)}^{1}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - 1\right)dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {\pi}^{2}\left[x{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right) d x - {∫}_{1}^{2}\left\{\dfrac{d}{dx}x{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right\}dx\right] - {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{\left[- \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1} + {\pi}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right \left(- cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left- {∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(- cos\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}{\left[cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{\left[- \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1} + {\pi}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right \left(- cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left+ {\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)}^{2}{\left[sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}{\left[cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$I = - {\pi}^{2}\left[\dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(0\right)\right] + {\pi}^{2}\left[2 \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(- cos\pi\right) + 1 \times \dfrac{2}{\pi} \times \left(cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right]\left+ 4\left[sin\left(\pi\right) - sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left[cos\left(\pi\right) - cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

$I = 2\pi + 4\pi + 4 ( 0 - 1 ) - 2\pi$

$I = 4\pi - 4$

$I = 4\left(\pi - 1\right)$

questions.q: Let $\left[t\right]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then the value of the integral ${∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left(\left[sin\left(\pix\right)\right] + {e}^{\left[cos\left(2\pix\right)\right]}\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, ${∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left(\left[sin\pix\right] + {e}^{\left[cos2\pix\right]}\right)dx$

Now let ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left[sin\pix\right]dx$ and ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- 3}^{101}{e}^{\left[cos2\pix\right]}dx$

Now checking periodicity of $\left[sin\pix\right]$ we get,

$0 < x < 1 ⇒ \left[sin\pix\right] = 0$

$1 < x < 2 ⇒ \left[sin\pix\right] = - 1$

$\left[sin\pix\right] \to$ periodic with period 2

So, ${I}_{1} = 52{∫}_{0}^{2}\left[sin\pix\right]dx$

$= 52\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}0 + {∫}_{1}^{2} - 1dx\right] = - 52$

Now checking periodicity of $\left[cos2\pix\right]$ we get,

$0 < x < \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{4} < x < \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = - 1$

$\dfrac{1}{2} < x < \dfrac{3}{4} ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = - 1$

$\dfrac{3}{4} < x < 1 ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = 0$

So, $\left[cos2\pix\right]$ has periodicity of $1$

So, ${I}_{2} = 104\left({∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{4}}{e}^{0}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{4}}^{\dfrac{3}{4}}{e}^{- 1}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{3}{4}}^{1}{e}^{0}dx\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = 104\left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{e} \times \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = 52 + \dfrac{52}{e}$

So, ${I}_{1} + {I}_{2} = \dfrac{52}{e}$ or ${∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left(\left[sin\pix\right] + {e}^{\left[cos2\pix\right]}\right)dx = \dfrac{52}{e}$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{e}^{cosx}sinx}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left({e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}\right)}dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx ⋅ {e}^{cosx}}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left({e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}\right)}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Using property of integral $\mathop{∫ f}_{a}^{b}\left(a + b - x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)$

we get $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx ⋅ {e}^{- cosx}}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left({e}^{- cosx} + {e}^{cosx}\right)}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding equation $\left(i\right)$ & $\left(ii\right)$ we get

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)} ⋅ \dfrac{\left({e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}\right)}{{e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}}dx$

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$ $⇒ 2I = 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$

Let $cosx = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

$I = - \mathop{∫}_{1}^{0}\dfrac{dt}{1 + {t}^{2}} ⇒ I = - {\left[\tan^{- 1}t\right]}_{1}^{0} = - \left[0 - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$ $= \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{{7}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}}dx$, where $\left[\cdot\right]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is equal to
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{dx}{{7}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}} = {∫}_{0}^{1}{\left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx$

Let $\dfrac{1}{7} = k ⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{1}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{3}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{4}}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx + ⋯$

$⇒ I = k\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + {k}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + {k}^{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) + ⋯$

$⇒ I = \left(k + \dfrac{{k}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{k}^{3}}{3} + ⋯\right) - \dfrac{1}{k}\left(\dfrac{{k}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{k}^{3}}{3} + ⋯\right)$

$⇒ I = - ln\left(1 - k\right) - \dfrac{1}{k}\left[- ln\left(1 - k\right) - k\right]$

$⇒ I = - ln\dfrac{6}{7} - 7\left[- ln\dfrac{6}{7} - \dfrac{1}{7}\right]\left(∵ k = \dfrac{1}{7}\right)$

$∴ I = 1 + 6ln\dfrac{6}{7}$

questions.q: The minimum value of the twice differentiable function $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}, x \in R$, is
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}{∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{- t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

$⇒ {e}^{- x}f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{- t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right)$

Differentiate on both side w.r.t $x$ we get,

${e}^{- x}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left(- f\left(x\right){e}^{- x}\right) = {e}^{- x}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) - 2x + 1$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2\right) + {e}^{x}\left(2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2x + 1\right) . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now finding critical point we get,

$2x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now differentiating equation $\left(1\right)$ to check maxima and minima we get,

${f}^{"}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2\right) + \left(2x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

$⇒ {f}^{"}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2x + 3\right)$

For $x = - \dfrac{1}{2}, {f}^{"}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) > 0$, so it will give point of minima,

Now minimum value will be given by, $f\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}\left(- 1 - 1\right) = - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{e}}$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a real valued continuous function on $\left[0, 1\right]$ and $f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(x - t\right)f\left(t\right)dt$. Then which of the following points $\left(x, y\right)$ lies on the curve $y = f\left(x\right)$?
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = x\left(1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(t\right)dt\right) - {∫}_{0}^{1}tf\left(t\right)dt$

$f\left(x\right) = Ax - B . . . \left(i\right)$

$A = 1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(t\right)dt = 1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(At - B\right)dt$

$⇒ A = 2\left(1 - B\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Also $B = {∫}_{0}^{1}tf\left(t\right)dt = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(A{t}^{2} - Bt\right)dt$

$A = \dfrac{9}{2}B . . . \left(iii\right)$

From $\left(ii\right), \left(iii\right)$

$A = \dfrac{18}{13}, B = \dfrac{4}{13}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{18}{13}x - \dfrac{4}{13}$

$⇒ f\left(6\right) = \dfrac{18 \times 6 - 4}{13} = 8$

questions.q: Let $\alpha \in \left(0, 1\right)$ and $\beta = {\log}_{e}\left(1 - \alpha\right)$. Let ${P}_{n}\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} + \ldots . + \dfrac{{x}^{n}}{n}, x \in \left(0, 1\right)$. Then the integral ${∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\dfrac{{t}^{50}}{1 - t}dt$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\dfrac{{t}^{50}}{1 - t}dt$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(\dfrac{1 - {t}^{50} - 1}{1 - t}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(\dfrac{1 - {t}^{50}}{1 - t}\right)dt + {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - t}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(1 + t + {t}^{2} + . . . + {t}^{49}\right)dt - {\left[ln\left(1 - t\right)\right]}_{0}^{\alpha}$

$⇒ I = - {\left[t + \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{t}^{3}}{3} + . . . + \dfrac{{t}^{50}}{50}\right]}_{0}^{\alpha} - ln\left(1 - \alpha\right)$

$⇒ I = - \left[\alpha + \dfrac{{\alpha}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{\alpha}^{3}}{3} + . . . + \dfrac{{\alpha}^{50}}{50}\right] - ln\left(1 - \alpha\right)$

$⇒ I = - \left(\beta + {P}_{50}\left(\alpha\right)\right)$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(2 + 3sinx\right)}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2 + 3sinx}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

Now rearranging the above integral we get,

$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{3}{\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{3}{\left(2\cos^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)} d x}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + \dfrac{3}{2}\mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) d x}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{2}}$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2\mathop{\mathop{{\left[tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right]}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{2}}$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

Now solving ${I}_{1}$ we get,

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{1}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{2tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{1 - tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left[1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}dx$

Put $tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = v ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx = dv$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}\dfrac{\left(1 + {v}^{2}\right)dv}{v}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\left[{\log}_{e}\left(v\right) + \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(1\right) - {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \dfrac{1}{3}$

So,

$I = \dfrac{1}{3} + {\log}_{e}\sqrt{3} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{10}{3} - \sqrt{3} + {\log}_{e}\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- {\log}_{e}2}^{{\log}_{e}2}{e}^{x}\left({\log}_{e}\left({e}^{x} + \sqrt{1 + {e}^{2x}}\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{- {\log}_{e}2}^{{\log}_{e}2}{e}^{x}\left[{\log}_{e}\left({e}^{x} + \sqrt{1 + {e}^{2x}}\right)\right]dx$

Let us substitute ${e}^{x} = t$

$⇒ {e}^{x}dx = dt$

Lower limit $= {e}^{- {\log}_{e}\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Upper limit $= {e}^{{\log}_{e}\left(2\right)} = 2$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2}1 \times {\log}_{e}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}\right]dt$

Apply integration by-parts.

$∫ u\left(t\right)v\left(t\right)dt = u\left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt - ∫ \left(u ' \left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt\right)dt$

Take $u\left(t\right) = {\log}_{e}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}\right], v\left(t\right) = 1$

$⇒ u ' \left(t\right) = \dfrac{1}{t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}}\left(1 + \dfrac{2t}{2\sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}}\right) = t$

$= {\left[tln\left(\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1} + x\right)\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2} - {∫}_{1 / 2}^{2}\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1}}dt$

$= {\left[tln\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1} + t - \sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2}$

$= \left[2ln\left(\sqrt{5} + 2\right) - \sqrt{5}\right] - \left[\dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\right]$

$= ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2} ( 2 + \sqrt{5}{)}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{5}}}\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$

Hence this is the correct option.

Let us substitute ${e}^{x} = t$

$⇒ {e}^{x}dx = dt$

Lower limit $= {e}^{- {\log}_{e}\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Upper limit $= {e}^{{\log}_{e}\left(2\right)} = 2$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2}1 \times {\log}_{e}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}\right]dt$

Apply integration by-parts.

$∫ u\left(t\right)v\left(t\right)dt = u\left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt - ∫ \left(u ' \left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt\right)dt$

Take $u\left(t\right) = {\log}_{e}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}\right], v\left(t\right) = 1$

$⇒ u ' \left(t\right) = \dfrac{1}{t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}}\left(1 + \dfrac{2t}{2\sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}}\right) = t$

$= {\left[tln\left(\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1} + x\right)\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2} - {∫}_{1 / 2}^{2}\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1}}dt$

$= {\left[tln\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1} + t - \sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2}$

$= \left[2ln\left(\sqrt{5} + 2\right) - \sqrt{5}\right] - \left[\dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\right]$

$= ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2} ( 2 + \sqrt{5}{)}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{5}}}\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$

Hence this is the correct option.

Then the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right)dx$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{min\left\{{x}^{2}, x - \left[x\right]\right\}}, & x \in [ 0, 1 ) \\ {e}^{\left[x - {\log}_{e}x\right]}, & x \in \left[1, 2\right]\end{cases}\right$
$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{{x}^{2}} & x \in [ 0, 1 ) \\ e, & x \in \left[1, 2\right]\end{cases}\right$

As $x - lnx \in [ 1, 2 )$ for $x \in [ 1, 2 ]$, so$\left[x - lnx\right] = 1$ and $x - \left[x\right] = \left\{x\right\}$, so $x \in \left(0, 1\right), {x}^{2} < \left\{x\right\}$

Now solving the integral we get,${∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{1}x \cdot {e}^{{x}^{2}}dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}x \cdot edx$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = 2e - \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: The minimum value of the function $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{\left|x - t\right|}dt$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{\left|x - t\right|}dt$

Now For $x \le 0$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{t - x}dt = {e}^{- x}\left({e}^{2} - 1\right)$

And for $0 < x < 2$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}dt + {∫}_{x}^{2}{e}^{t - x}dt = {e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x} - 2$

For $x \ge 2$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{x - t}dt = {e}^{x - 2}\left({e}^{2} - 1\right)$

Now for $x \le 0, f\left(x\right)$ is decreasing as ${e}^{- x}$ is decreasing function and $x \ge 2, f\left(x\right)$ is increasing as ${e}^{x - 2}$ is increasing function,

So, minimum value of $f\left(x\right)$ lies in $x \in \left(0, 2\right)$

Applying A.M $\ge$ G.M in ${e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x}$we get,

$\dfrac{{e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x}}{2} \ge \sqrt{{e}^{x} \times {e}^{2 - x}}$

$⇒ {e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x} \ge 2e$

Hence, the minimum value of $f\left(x\right)$ is $2e - 2 = 2\left(e - 1\right)$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ satisfies the equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \left|A\right| = 0,$ for all $x > 0,$ where $A = \left[\begin{cases}y & sinx & 1 \\ 0 & - 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & \dfrac{1}{x}\end{cases}\right]$. If $y ( \pi ) = \pi + 2,$ then the value of $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
We have,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}y & sinx & 1 \\ 0 & - 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & \dfrac{1}{x}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = - \dfrac{y}{x} + 2sinx + 2$

Now,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left|A\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{y}{x} + 2sinx + 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = 2sinx + 2$

$\text{I.F.} = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = x$

Solution is

$y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ \left(I . F .\right) \times \left(2sinx + 2\right)dx$

$⇒ yx = ∫ x ( 2sinx + 2 ) dx$

$⇒ yx = 2 ∫ x\left(sinx\right)dx + 2 ∫ xdx$

$⇒ xy = {x}^{2} - 2xcosx + 2sinx + c \ldots \left(i\right)$

Now $x = \pi, y = \pi + 2$, hence

$⇒ \pi\left(\pi + 2\right) = {\pi}^{2} - 2\pi\left(- 1\right) + 0 + c$

$⇒ c = 0$

Now $\left(i\right)$ becomes

$xy = {x}^{2} - 2xcosx + 2sinx$

Put $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then

$\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)y = {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2} - 2 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2}cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 2sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)y = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} + 2$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{4}{\pi}$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)dy = \left(y + y{x}^{2} - 3{x}^{4}\right)dx, x > 2$ If $y\left(3\right) = 3,$ then $y\left(4\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)dy = \left(y + y{x}^{2} - 3{x}^{4}\right)dx$

$⇒ xdy - ydx = \left(y{x}^{2} - 3{x}^{4}\right)dx + {x}^{3}dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{{x}^{2}} = ( ydx + xdy ) - 3{x}^{2}dx$

$⇒ d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = d\left(xy\right) - d\left({x}^{3}\right)$

Integrate

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} = xy - {x}^{3} + c$

given $f\left(3\right) = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{3} = 3 \times 3 - {3}^{3} + c$

$⇒ c = 19$

$∴ \dfrac{y}{x} = xy - {x}^{3} + 19$

at $x = 4, \dfrac{y}{4} = 4y - 64 + 19$

$15y = 4 \times 45$

$⇒ y = 12$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x + y} - {2}^{x}}{{2}^{y}}, y\left(0\right) = 1,$ then $y ( 1 )$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given that

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x + y} - {2}^{x}}{{2}^{y}} = {2}^{x}\left(\dfrac{{2}^{y} - 1}{{2}^{y}}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{{2}^{y}}{{2}^{y} - 1}\right)dy = {2}^{x}dx$

By using Variable Separable method

$∫ \dfrac{{2}^{y}dy}{{2}^{y} - 1} = ∫ {2}^{x}dx$

Let ${2}^{y} - 1 = t ⇒ {2}^{y}ln\left(2\right)dy = dt$

$∫ \dfrac{dt}{t}\dfrac{1}{ℓn2} = ∫ {2}^{x}dx$

We know that $∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx = ln\left(x\right) + c \text{ and } ∫ {a}^{x}dx = \dfrac{{a}^{x}}{ln\left(a\right)} + c .$

$⇒ \dfrac{ln\left(t\right)}{ln\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{{2}^{x}}{ln\left(2\right)} + \dfrac{c}{ln\left(2\right)}$

$⇒ ln\left(t\right) = {2}^{x} + c$

$⇒ ln\left({2}^{y} - 1\right) = {2}^{x} + c$

when $x = 0, y = 1 ⇒ ln\left(2 - 1\right) = {2}^{0} + c$

$⇒ c = - 1 .$

$⇒ ln\left({2}^{y} - 1\right) = {2}^{x} - 1$

$⇒ {2}^{y} - 1 = {e}^{{2}^{x} - 1}$

$⇒ {2}^{y} = 1 + {e}^{{2}^{x} - 1}$

when $x = 1 ⇒ {2}^{y} = 1 + {e}^{1} ⇒ y = {\log}_{2} ( 1 + e )$

We get, $\dfrac{\pi}{4} + lnx = \tan^{- 1}\left(xy\right)$

$xy = \left(\dfrac{1 + tan\left(ℓnx\right)}{1 - tan\left(ℓnx\right)}\right) ⋯ \left(ii\right)$

Put $x = e$ in $\left(ii\right)$

We get,$e . y\left(e\right) = \dfrac{1 + tan1}{1 - tan1}$

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\left(x - {y}^{2}\right)dx + y\left(5x + {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\left(x - {y}^{2}\right)dx + y\left(5x + {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$

After rearranging we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{y}^{2} - x}{y\left(5x + {y}^{2}\right)}$

Now, let ${y}^{2} = v ⇒ 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$\dfrac{1}{2y}\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v - x}{y\left(5x + v\right)}$

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 2\left(\dfrac{v - x}{5x + v}\right)$

Now let $v = kx$

$⇒ k + x\dfrac{dk}{dx} = 2\left(\dfrac{kx - x}{5x + kx}\right)$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dk}{dx} = - \dfrac{\left({k}^{2} + 3k + 2\right)}{k + 5}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{\left(5 + k\right)}{\left(k + 1\right)\left(k + 2\right)}dk = ∫ - \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{4}{k + 1} - \dfrac{3}{k + 2}\right)dk = - ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ 4ln\left(k + 1\right) - 3ln\left(k + 2\right) = - lnx + lnc$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(k + 1\right)}^{4}}{{\left(k + 2\right)}^{3}} = \dfrac{c}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{v}{x} + 1\right)}^{4}}{{\left(\dfrac{v}{x} + 2\right)}^{3}} = \dfrac{c}{x}$

$⇒ c{\left({y}^{2} + 2x\right)}^{3} = {\left({y}^{2} + x\right)}^{4}$

$d\left(\dfrac{y}{x + 1}\right) = {e}^{3x}dx$

So $C = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{\left(x + 1\right){e}^{3x}}{3}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{e}^{3x}}{3}\left(3x + 4\right)$

$\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = {e}^{3x}\left(3x + 5\right)$

Clearly, $x = \dfrac{- 4}{3}$ is a point of local minima as ${\left(\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}\right)}_{x = \dfrac{- 4}{3}} < 0$

$2{e}^{- 4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right),$ with $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = {e}^{- \pi}$, then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $\left(\sin^{2}2x\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(8\sin^{2}2x + 2sin4x\right)y =$

$2{e}^{- 4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)$

Now rewriting the given differential equation we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(8 + 4cot2x\right)y = \dfrac{2{e}^{- 4x}}{\sin^{2}2x}\left(2sinx + cos2x\right)$

Which is a linear differential equation.

Now calculating $IF = {e}^{∫ \left(8 + 4cot2x\right)dx} = {e}^{8x + 2ln\left(sin2x\right)}$

Now solution of differential equation is given by,

$⇒ y\left({e}^{8x} \cdot \sin^{2}2x\right) = ∫ 2{e}^{4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)dx$

$⇒ y\left({e}^{8x} \cdot \sin^{2}2x\right) = {e}^{4x} \cdot sin2x + C$

Now given $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = {e}^{- \pi} ⇒ C = 0$

So, the equation of curve is given by $y = \dfrac{{e}^{- 4x}}{sin2x}$

Then $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $x\left(\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} - {y}^{2}}} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\left(\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} - {y}^{2}}} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + x$

Taking $x$ common & cancelling them we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{2}}} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \dfrac{y}{x}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{2}}} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + 1$

Let $y = vx$$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$\left(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {v}^{2}}} + {e}^{v}\right) = v\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {v}^{2}}} + {e}^{v}\right) + 1$

$v + x\dfrac{dV}{dx} = v + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {v}^{2}}} + {e}^{v}\right)}$

$x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {v}^{2}}} + {e}^{v}\right)}$ $⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {v}^{2}}} + {e}^{v}\right)dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}$

Integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {v}^{2}}} + {e}^{v}\right)dv = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}v + {e}^{v} = lnx + c$ $⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + e\dfrac{y}{x} = lnx + c$

Now $y\left(1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{0}{1}\right) + {e}^{0} = ln1 + c$

$⇒ c = 1$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + e\dfrac{y}{x} = lnx + 1$ ........(i)

Now $y\left(2\alpha\right) = \alpha$ putting in equation (i) we get,

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2\alpha}\right) + e\dfrac{\alpha}{2\alpha} = ln2\alpha + 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{6} + e\dfrac{1}{2} = ln2\alpha + 1$ $⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{\dfrac{\pi}{6} + \sqrt{e} - 1}$

questions.solution:
Given,

$2ye\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}dx + \left({y}^{2} - 4xe\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}\right)dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}\left[ydx - 2xdy\right] + {y}^{2}dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}\left[\dfrac{{y}^{2}dx - x \cdot \left(2y\right)dy}{y}\right] + {y}^{2}dy = 0$

Divide by ${y}^{3}$

$2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}\left[\dfrac{{y}^{2}dx - x \cdot \left(2y\right)dy}{{y}^{4}}\right] + \dfrac{1}{y}dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}d\left(\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}\right) + \dfrac{1}{y}dy = 0$

Now integrating both side we get,

$∫ 2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}d\left(\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}}\right) + ∫ \dfrac{1}{y}dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}} + lny + c = 0$

Given, $\left(0, 1\right)$ lies on it,

So, $2{e}^{0} + ln1 + c = 0 ⇒ c = - 2$

Hence required curve: $2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}} + lny - 2 = 0$

For $x\left(e\right)$

$2e\dfrac{x}{{e}^{2}} + lne - 2 = 0 ⇒ x = - {e}^{2}{\log}_{e}2$

questions.q: If the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y}$ passes through the point $\left(2, 1\right)$ and $\left(k + 1, 2\right), k > 0$, then
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y} = \dfrac{\left(x - 1\right) + \left(y - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) - \left(y - 1\right)}$

Now let $x - 1 = X, y - 1 = Y$

So, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{X + Y}{X - Y} . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now let $Y = VX\dfrac{dY}{dX} = V + X\dfrac{dV}{dX}$

Putting the value in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$V + X\dfrac{dV}{dX} = \dfrac{1 + V}{1 - V}$

$⇒ X\dfrac{dV}{dX} = \dfrac{{V}^{2} + 1}{1 - V}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{1 - V}{1 + {V}^{2}}dV = ∫ \dfrac{dX}{X}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dV}{1 + {V}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{2VdV}{1 + {V}^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{dX}{X}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}V - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 + {V}^{2}\right) = lnX + c$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{Y}{X}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 + \dfrac{{Y}^{2}}{{X}^{2}}\right) = ln\left(X\right) + c$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 1}{x - 1}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 + \dfrac{{\left(y - 1\right)}^{2}}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}}\right) = ln\left(x - 1\right) + c$

Now given curve passes through $\left(2, 1\right)$

So, $0 - \dfrac{1}{2}ln1 = ln1 + c ⇒ c = 0$

Now given curve also passes through $\left(k + 1, 2\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{{x}^{3} + 6{x}^{2} + 11x + 6}\right)y = \dfrac{x + 3}{x + 1}$

We get $p\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{{x}^{3} + 6{x}^{2} + 11x + 6}$

So $IF = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{{x}^{3} + 6{x}^{2} + 11x + 6}dx}$

Now finding the integration we get,

$∫ p\left(x\right)dx = ∫ \dfrac{\left(2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13\right)dx}{\left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 2\right)\left(x + 3\right)}$

Using partial fraction we get,

$\dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{\left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 2\right)\left(x + 3\right)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 2} + \dfrac{C}{x + 3}$

On solving we get $A = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$, $B = 1$ and $C = - 1$

So, $∫ p\left(x\right)dx = Aln\left(x + 1\right) + Bln\left(x + 2\right) + cln\left(x + 3\right)$

$= ln\left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right)$

So, $IF = {e}^{∫ p\left(x\right)dx} = \dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x + 3\right)}$

Now solution of differential equation is given by

$y \times IF = ∫ Q \times IFdx$

$⇒ y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right) = ∫ \left(\dfrac{x + 3}{x + 1}\right)\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x + 3\right)}dx$

$⇒ y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3{x}^{2}}{2} + 2x + c$

Now given curve passes through $\left(0, 1\right)$,

So, $⇒ 1 \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(0 + 1\right)}^{2}\left(0 + 2\right)}{0 + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{0}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3 \times {0}^{2}}{2} + 2 \times 0 + c ⇒ c = \dfrac{2}{3}$

So, curve becomes $y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3{x}^{2}}{2} + 2x + \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now put $x = 1$ we get, $y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(1 + 1\right)}^{2}\left(1 + 2\right)}{1 + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{1}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3 \times {1}^{2}}{2} + 2 \times 1 + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ y \times 3 = 1 + \dfrac{3}{2} + 2 ⇒ y \times 3 = \dfrac{9}{2}$

$⇒ y\left(1\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ c = 0$

Put $x = a, y = 2$

$3 = {e}^{c}{e}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{du}{dv} + \dfrac{1}{2vlnv} . u = \dfrac{1}{v}$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{14}{3}$

Put $x = \sin^{2}\theta, 0 < x < 1$

$sin\theta = \sqrt{x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = cos\left(2\tan^{- 1}sin\left({cot}^{- 1}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \sin^{2}\theta}{\sin^{2}\theta}}\right)\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = cos\left(2\tan^{- 1} ( sin\theta )\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = cos\left(2\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}\left(\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x}\right)}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)\left(- 1\right) - \left(1 - x\right) \cdot 1}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 2}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}$

Multiply, ${\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}$ on both sides

$⇒ {\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 2{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}$

Now, $2{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{2{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}$

$∴ {\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) + 2{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} = 0$ option $\left(1\right)$ satisfied

questions.q: If $y ( x ) = {cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + sinx} + \sqrt{1 - sinx}}{\sqrt{1 + sinx} - \sqrt{1 - sinx}}\right), x \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ is:
questions.solution:
$y ( x ) = {cot}^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + sin ⁡ x} + \sqrt{1 - sin ⁡ x}}{\sqrt{1 + sin ⁡ x} - \sqrt{1 - sin ⁡ x}}$

As we know that, $\sqrt{1 - sin ⁡ x} = \left|sin\dfrac{x}{2} - cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right| \text{ and } \sqrt{1 + sin ⁡ x} = \left|sin\dfrac{x}{2} + cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right|$

$y ( x ) = {cot}^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{\left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right| + \left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right|}{\left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right| - \left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right|}$

$= {cot}^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}{cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}\text{for}x \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)$

$= {cot}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(\dfrac{sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}{cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}\right)$

$= {cot}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(tan ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right)$

$= {cot}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(cot ⁡ ( \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{x}{2} )\right)$

$y ( x ) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{x}{2}$

${y}^{′} ( x ) = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} + x - 5$. If $g\left(x\right)$ is a function such that $f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = x, ∀ x \in R$, then ${g}^{'}\left(63\right)$ is equal to ______
questions.solution:
Here, $g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = x$ as $f\left(x\right)$ and $g\left(x\right)$ are inverse of each other.

Now, ${g}^{'}\left(f\left(x\right)\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 1$

$⇒ {g}^{'}\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)} \ldots \left(i\right)$

Now $f\left(x\right) = 63 ⇒ {x}^{3} + x - 5 = 63$

$⇒ {x}^{3} + x - 68 = 0$

So $x = 4$ satisfies the above equation

${g}^{'}\left(63\right) = \dfrac{1}{{f}^{'}\left(4\right)}$ from $\left(i\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{3{\left(4\right)}^{2} + 1} = \dfrac{1}{49}$

questions.q: Let $x\left(t\right) = 2\sqrt{2}cost\sqrt{sin2t}$ and $y\left(t\right) = 2\sqrt{2}sint\sqrt{sin2t}, t \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Then $\dfrac{1 + {\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2}}{\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{{dx}^{2}}}$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given

$x = 2\sqrt{2}cost\sqrt{sin2t}$

Now differentiating w.r.t $t$ both side we get,

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}cos3t}{\sqrt{sin2t}} . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also given $y\left(t\right) = 2\sqrt{2}sint\sqrt{sin2t}$

Again differentiating w.r.t $t$ both side we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}sin3t}{\sqrt{sin2t}} . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now dividing equation $\left(2\right)$ from $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = tan3t$

Now finding the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - 1$

Now finding $\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ we get,

$\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{{sec}^{2}3t \cdot \sqrt{sin2t}}{cos3t}$

Now finding value of $\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ we get,

$\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = - 3$

Now putting the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} \text{ and } \dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ in$\dfrac{1 + {\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2}}{\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}}$ we get,

$\dfrac{1 + {\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2}}{\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}} = \dfrac{1 + 1}{- 3} = - \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q: Let $f, g: N \to N$ such that $f\left(n + 1\right) = f\left(n\right) + f\left(1\right) ∀ n \in N$ and $g$ be any arbitrary function. Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: If $f$ is onto, then $f\left(n\right) = n ∀ n \in N$
If $g$ is onto, then $fog$ is one-one
If $fog$ is one-one, then $g$ is one-one
questions.solution:
$f\left(n + 1\right) - f\left(n\right) = f\left(1\right)$

A.P. with common difference = $f ( 1 )$

General term = ${T}_{n} = f ( 1 ) + ( n - 1 ) f ( 1 ) = nf ( 1 )$

$⇒ f\left(n\right) = nf\left(1\right)$$⇒ f$ is one-one

Now, Let $f\left(g\left({x}_{2}\right)\right) = f\left(g\left({x}_{1}\right)\right)$

$⇒ g\left({x}_{2}\right) = g\left({x}_{1}\right)$ (as $f$ is one-one)

$⇒ {x}_{1} = {x}_{2}$ (as $fog$ is one-one)

$⇒ g$ is one-one

For $f$ to be onto, $f ( n )$ should take all the values of natural numbers.

As $f ( x )$ is increasing, $f ( 1 ) = 1$

$⇒ f ( n ) = n$

Now, $f\left(g\left(n\right)\right) = g\left(n\right)f\left(1\right)$

may be many-one if

$g\left(n\right)$ is many-one

So “if $g$ is onto, then $fog$ is one-one” is incorrect.

Let $A = \left\{1, 2, 3, \ldots , 10\right\}$ and $f: A \to A$ be defined as

$f\left(k\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}k + 1 & ifkis odd \\ k & ifkis even\end{cases}\right$

Then the number of possible functions $g: A \to A$ such that $gof = f$ is:
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}x + 1 & ifxis odd \\ x & ifxis even\end{cases}\right$

$∵ g: A \to$ A such that $g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = f\left(x\right)$

$⇒$ If $x$ is even then $g\left(x\right) = x \ldots \left(1\right)$

If $x$ is odd then $g\left(x + 1\right) = x + 1 \ldots \left(2\right)$

from $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$ we can say that $g\left(x\right) = x$ if $x$ is even

$⇒$ If $x$ is odd then $g\left(x\right)$ can take any value in set $A$

so number of $g\left(x\right) = {10}^{5} \times 1$

Thus $f\left(k\right) = 1$

questions.q: The total number of functions, $f: \left\{1, 2, 3, 4\right\} \to \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\right\}$ such that $f\left(1\right) + f\left(2\right) = f\left(3\right)$, is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $f\left(1\right) + f\left(2\right) = f\left(3\right)$

Now possible values of $f\left(3\right)$ are $2, 3, 4, 5$ and $6$ (it cannot be $1$ as minimum value $f\left(1\right) \text{ and } f\left(2\right)$ is $1$, so $1 + 1 = 2$ )

For each $k$, if $f\left(3\right) = k$ then there will be $\left(k - 1\right)$ set of values for $f\left(1\right)$ and $f\left(2\right)$

For example if $f\left(3\right) = 3$ then possible value of $f\left(1\right) \text{ and } f\left(2\right)$ will be $\left(1, 2\right)\text{or}\left(2, 1\right) ⇒$ $2$ values

Similarly for $f\left(3\right) = 4$, possible values will be $\left(1, 3\right), \left(3, 1\right), \left(2, 2\right) ⇒$$3$ values.

And so on.

So number of possible combinations of $f\left(1\right), f\left(2\right)$ and $f\left(3\right)$ are $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be a continuous function such that $f\left(3x\right) - f\left(x\right) = x$. If $f\left(8\right) = 7$, then $f\left(14\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $f\left(3x\right) - f\left(x\right) = x$

Now replance $x\text{by}\dfrac{x}{3}$ infinite times,

$f\left(x\right) - f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) = \dfrac{x}{3}$

$f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) - f\left(\dfrac{x}{{3}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{x}{{3}^{2}} . .$

On adding, we get

$f\left(x\right) - \lim_{n \to \infty}f\left(\dfrac{x}{{3}^{n}}\right) = x\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{{3}^{2}} + ⋯ + \infty\right)$

$f\left(x\right) - \lim_{n \to \infty}f\left(\dfrac{x}{{3}^{n}}\right) = x\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{3}}\right) = \dfrac{x}{2}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) - f\left(0\right) = \dfrac{x}{2}$

Given $f\left(8\right) = 7$

so $f\left(8\right) - f\left(0\right) = 4$

i.e. $f\left(0\right) = 3$

$∴ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{2} + 3$

Hence $f\left(14\right) = 10$

questions.q: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = x - 1$  and $g: R \to \left\{1, - 1\right\} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined as $g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2} - 1}$. Then the function $fog$ is:
questions.solution:
$fog\left(x\right) = f\left(g\left(x\right)\right)$ $= f\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2} + 1}\right)$

$= \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2} + 1} - 1$ $= \dfrac{{x}^{2} - {x}^{2} - 1}{{x}^{2} + 1}$ $= \dfrac{- 1}{{x}^{2} + 1}$

We know that, $0 \le {x}^{2} < \infty , ∀ x \in R$

$⇒ 1 \le {x}^{2} + 1 < \infty , ∀ x \in R$ $⇒ 1 \ge \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2} + 1} > 0, ∀ x \in R$ $⇒ - 1 \le \dfrac{- 1}{{x}^{2} + 1} < 0, ∀ x \in R$

So, range of $fog\left(x\right)$ is $\left[- 1, 0\right) ⊂ R$.

Hence, the function $fog\left(x\right)$ is into function and $fog\left(- x\right) = f\left(g\left(- x\right)\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{{\left(- x\right)}^{2} + 1} = \dfrac{- 1}{{x}^{2} + 1} = f\left(g\left(x\right)\right)$

$∴ fog\left(x\right)$ is an even function. So, it is a many one function.

Hence, $fog\left(x\right)$ is neither one-one nor onto function.

Given,

Mean is zero, so $\dfrac{{a}_{1} + {a}_{2} + {a}_{3} + \ldots . . + {a}_{n}}{n} = 0$

Now this means that first and last term, second and second last and so on are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign.

Given, $f\left(x\right) = \alpha{x}^{5} + \beta{x}^{3} + \gammax$

Now finding $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}f\left({a}_{i}\right) = \alpha\left({a}_{1}^{5} + {a}_{2}^{5} + {a}_{3}^{5} + \ldots . + {a}_{n}^{5}\right) + \beta\left({a}_{1}^{3} + {a}_{2}^{3} + \ldots . + {a}_{n}^{3}\right) + \gamma\left({a}_{1} + {a}_{2} + \ldots . + {a}_{n}\right)$

Now given $g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = x$

$⇒ f\left(g\left(f\left(x\right)\right)\right) = f\left(x\right)$

So, $f\left(g\left(\dfrac{1}{n}\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}f\left({a}_{i}\right)\right)\right] = \dfrac{1}{n}\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}f\left({a}_{i}\right) = 0$ {from equation$\left(1\right)$ }

questions.q: The equation ${x}^{2} – 4x + [ x ] + 3 = x [ x ]$, where $[ x ]$ denotes the greatest integer function, has:
questions.solution:
Given:

${x}^{2} - 4x + \left[x\right] + 3 = x\left[x\right]$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 4x + 3 = x\left[x\right] - \left[x\right]$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 3\right) = \left[x\right]\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ x = 1$ or $x - 3 = \left[x\right]$

If $x - 3 = \left[x\right]$

$⇒ x – \left[x\right] = 3$

$⇒ \left\{x\right\} = 3$

which is not Possible, since $\left\{x\right\} \in [ 0, 1 )$.

Hence, $x = 1$ is the only one solution in $\left(- \infty , \infty\right)$.

questions.solution:

$⇒ f\left(1\right) + 2f\left(2\right) + 3f\left(3\right) + \ldots + \left(x - 1\right)f\left(x - 1\right) = x\left(x - 1\right)f\left(x - 1\right)$

Now when $x = 2$, then

$⇒ 1 = 4f\left(2\right)$

$⇒ f\left(2\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}$

So,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2x}$

Hence,

$\dfrac{1}{f\left(2022\right)} + \dfrac{1}{f\left(2028\right)} = 4044 + 4056 = 8100$

questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{\betax} - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}{\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{\deltax} + C$

Now let $I = ∫ \left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)lnxdx$

Now let ${\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} = t$

$⇒ 2x\left(lnx - 1\right) = lnt$

$⇒ lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{2t}dt$

So, $I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)\dfrac{dt}{t}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + c$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} - {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right) + C$

Now on comparing with $I = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{\betax} - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}{\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{\deltax} + C$, we get $\alpha = 2, \beta = 2, \gamma = 2, \delta = 2$

Hence, $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta = 2 + 4 + 6 - 8 = 4$

Hence this is the required option.

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{{n}^{2}},$ where $r$ is non-zero real number and $\left[r\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $r,$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
We know that $r \le \left[r\right] < r + 1$

$2r \le \left[2r\right] < 2r + 1$

$3r \le \left[3r\right] < 3r + 1$

$⋮ ⋮ ⋮$

$nr \le \left[nr\right] < nr + 1$

On adding all the above inequalities, we get

$r + 2r + \ldots + nr \le \left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right] < r + 2r + . . . nr + n$

Using $1 + 2 + 3 + . . . + n = \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}, n \in N,$

$\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r \le \left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right] < \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r}{{n}^{2}} \le \dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{{n}^{2}} < \dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n}{{n}^{2}}$

Now, $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{n ( n + 1 ) \cdot r}{2 \cdot {n}^{2}} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{n}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) \cdot r}{2 \cdot {n}^{2}} = \dfrac{r}{2}$

and $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n}{{n}^{2}} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{n}^{2}\left\{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) \cdot r + \dfrac{1}{n}\right\}}{2 \cdot {n}^{2}} = \dfrac{r}{2}$

So, by Sandwich Theorem, we can conclude that

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{{n}^{2}} = \dfrac{r}{2} .$

questions.q: If $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\sqrt{{n}^{2} - n - 1} + n\alpha + \beta\right) = 0$ then $8\left(\alpha + \beta\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $\lim_{n \to \infty}\sqrt{{n}^{2} - n - 1} + \alphan + \beta = 0$

Now rewriting the expression we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\left({n}^{2} - n - 1\right)\dfrac{1}{2} + \alphan = - \beta$

$⇒$$\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} + \alphan = - \beta$

Now on using binomial approximation ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{n} = 1 + nx$ we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2n} - \dfrac{1}{2{n}^{2}}\right) + \alphan = - \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}n - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} + \alphan = - \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 + \alpha\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} = - \beta$

Now for limit to exist $\left(1 + \alpha\right) = 0 ⇒ \alpha = - 1$

Now on putting the value of $\alpha$ we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 + \alpha\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} = - \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty} - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} = - \beta$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2} - 0 = - \beta$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So, $8\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = 8\left(- 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 8 \times \dfrac{- 1}{2} = - 4$

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\left({n}^{2} - n - 1\right)\dfrac{1}{2} + \alphan = - \beta$

$⇒$$\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} + \alphan = - \beta$

Now on using binomial approximation ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{n} = 1 + nx$ we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2n} - \dfrac{1}{2{n}^{2}}\right) + \alphan = - \beta$

Now for limit to exist $\left(1 + \alpha\right) = 0 ⇒ \alpha = - 1$

Now on putting the value of $\alpha$ we get,

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty} - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} = - \beta$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2} - 0 = - \beta$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So, $8\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = 8\left(- 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 8 \times \dfrac{- 1}{2} = - 4$

Consider $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{cos ( sinx ) - cosx}{{x}^{4}}\left(\dfrac{0}{0}\text{form}\right)$

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{2sin\left(\dfrac{sinx + x}{2}\right) \cdot sin\left(\dfrac{x - sinx}{2}\right)}{{x}^{4}}$

$\lim_{x \to 0}2\left[\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{sinx + x}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{sinx + x}{2}\right)}\right]\left[\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{x - sinx}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{x - sinx}{2}\right)}\right] \times \left(\dfrac{{x}^{2} - \sin^{2}x}{4{x}^{4}}\right)$

$\lim_{x \to 0}2 \times \left(\dfrac{{x}^{2} - \sin^{2}x}{4{x}^{4}}\right)\left(\dfrac{0}{0}\text{form}\right)\left(∵ \lim_{t \to 0}\dfrac{sint}{t} = 1\right)$

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{2 - 2cos2x}{24{x}^{2}}\right)\left(\dfrac{0}{0}\text{form}\right)$

questions.q: Let $\beta = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax - \left({e}^{3x} - 1\right)}{\alphax\left({e}^{3x} - 1\right)}$ for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ is:
questions.solution:
Given, $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax - \left({e}^{3x} - 1\right)}{\alphax\left({e}^{3x} - 1\right)} = \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax + 1 - {e}^{3x}}{\dfrac{\alphax\left({e}^{3x} - 1\right)}{3x} \cdot 3x} = \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax + 1 - {e}^{3x}}{3\alpha{x}^{2}} = \beta$ as $\left(\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{e}^{x} - 1}{x} = 1\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha - 3{e}^{3x}}{6\alphax} = \beta$ [Using L' Hospital rule as $\left(\dfrac{0}{0}\text{form}\right)$]

Now for limit to exist, $\alpha = 3$

So, $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{3 - 3{e}^{3x}}{6 \times 3 \times x} = \beta$

So, $\beta = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- \left({e}^{3x} - 1\right)}{6x} = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- 3{e}^{3x}}{6} = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ \alpha + \beta = \dfrac{5}{2}$

questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x\sin^{2}x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in R$, then which of the following is NOT correct?
questions.solution:
Given,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x\sin^{2}x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{{x}^{3}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{{x}^{2}}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{{x}^{3}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now using expansion of given function in terms of $x$ we get,

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha\left(1 + x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3 !} + \ldots\right) + \beta\left(1 - x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3 !} + \ldots\right) + \gamma\left(x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3 !} + \ldots\right)}{{x}^{3}}$

Now for limit to exist constant terms should be zero

$⇒ a + \beta = 0 . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also coefficient of $x$ should be zero

$⇒ \alpha - \beta + \gamma = 0 . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Also coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ should be zero

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha}{2} + \dfrac{\beta}{2} = 0 . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

So limit becomes, $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{x}^{3}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{3 !} - \dfrac{\beta}{3 !} - \dfrac{\gamma}{3 !}\right) + {x}^{4}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{3 !} - \dfrac{\beta}{3 !} - \dfrac{\gamma}{3 !}\right)}{{x}^{3}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now putting the value of limit we get,

$\dfrac{\alpha}{6} - \dfrac{\beta}{6} - \dfrac{\gamma}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . . . . . . \left(4\right)$

Now on solving equation $1, 2, 3 \text{ and } 4$ we get,

$⇒ \alpha = 1, \beta = - 1, \gamma = - 2$

Now putting these in all option we get, $\alpha{\beta}^{2} + \beta{\gamma}^{2} + \gamma{\alpha}^{2} + 3 = 0$

left(a + b\right)}^{n}$ and ${\left(a - b\right)}^{n}$ is given by,

${\left(a + b\right)}^{n} = C0 n {a}^{n}{b}^{0} + C1 n {a}^{n - 1}{b}^{1} + C2 n {a}^{n - 2}{b}^{2} + . . . . . . + Cn n {a}^{0}{b}^{n}$

${\left(a - b\right)}^{n} = C0 n {a}^{n}{b}^{0} - C1 n {a}^{n - 1}{b}^{1} + C2 n {a}^{n - 2}{b}^{2} - . . . . . . + Cn n {a}^{0}{b}^{n}$

So, ${\left(a + b\right)}^{6} + {\left(a - b\right)}^{6} = 2\left({T}_{1} + {T}_{3} + {T}_{5} + {T}_{7}\right)$

$= 2\left(C0 6 {a}^{6} + C2 6 {a}^{4}{b}^{2} + c4 6 {a}^{2}{b}^{4} + C6 6 {b}^{6}\right)$

From equation (1) we get,

$\lim_{x \to \infty}\dfrac{\left(2{\left(3x + 1\right)}^{3} + 30{\left(3x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(3x - 1\right) + 30\left(3x + 1\right){\left(3x - 1\right)}^{2} + 2{\left(3x - 1\right)}^{3}\right)}{2{x}^{6} + 30{x}^{4}\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) + 30{x}^{2}{\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)}^{3}}$

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let,

$L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\}$

Now,

$2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3} < 1$

$2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5} < 1$

--------------------

$2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1} < 1 ∀ n \in N$

And ${\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} < \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right) < {\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n}$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} < \lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\} < \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n}$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} < L < \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n}$

And $\lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} = 0 \text{ and } \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n} = 0$

$\left\{\text{as}2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3} < 1 \text{ and } 2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1} < 1\right\}$

Hence, $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\} = 0$

Given that

We know that ${e}^{ax} = 1 + ax + \dfrac{( ax{)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots$ and $cos\left(bx\right) = 1 - \dfrac{( bx{)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots$

questions.q: Define a relation $R$ over a class of $n \times n$ real matrices $A$ and $B$ as "$ARB$ iff there exists a non-singular matrix $P$ such that $PA{P}^{- 1} = B$". Then which of the following is true ?
options: $R$ is symmetric, transitive but not reflexive
$R$ is reflexive, symmetric but not transitive
$R$ is reflexive, transitive but not symmetric
questions.solution:
Given $A$ and $B$ are matrices of $n \times n$ order and $ARB$ iff there exists a non-singular matrix $P\left(det \left(P\right) \ne 0\right)$ such that $PA{P}^{- 1} = B$.

Reflexivity Check :

$ARA ⇒ PA{P}^{- 1} = A$ which is true for $P = I$.

So, $R$ is reflexive relation.

Symmetric Check :

$ARB ⇒ PA{P}^{- 1} = B ⇒ {P}^{- 1}PA{P}^{- 1}P = {P}^{- 1}BP ⇒ IAI = {P}^{- 1}BP ⇒ {P}^{- 1}BP = A ⇒ BRA$ for matrix ${P}^{- 1}$.

So, $R$ is symmetric relation.

Transitivity Check :

$ARB ⇒ PA{P}^{- 1} = B$ and $BRC ⇒ PB{P}^{- 1} = C$.

So, $PPA{P}^{- 1}{P}^{- 1} = C$.

$⇒ {P}^{2}A{\left({P}^{2}\right)}^{- 1} = C ⇒ ARC$

So, $R$ is a transitive relation.

Since, $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive all.

Hence, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

Let $Z$ be the set of all integers,

Relation from $A ∩ B$ to $A ∩ C = {2}^{5 \times 5} = {2}^{p}$

$⇒ p = 25$

questions.q: Let $P\left(S\right)$ denote the power set of $S = \left\{1, 2, 3, \ldots , 10\right\}$. Define the relations ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ on $P\left(S\right)$ as $A{R}_{1}B$ if $\left(A ∩ {B}^{c}\right) ∪ \left(B ∩ {A}^{c}\right) = ϕ$ and $A{R}_{2}B$ if $A ∪ {B}^{c} = B ∪ {A}^{c}, ∀ A, B \in P\left(S\right)$ . Then :
options: both ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are not equivalence relations
questions.solution:
Given,

$S = \left\{1, 2, 3, \ldots \ldots 10\right\}$

$P\left(S\right) =$ power set of $S$

$A{R}_{1}B ⇒ \left(A ∩ {B}^{c}\right) ∪ \left({A}^{c} ∩ B\right) = ϕ$

Now for reflexive property, replacing $B$ with $A$ we get,

$\left(A ∩ {A}^{c}\right) ∪ \left({A}^{c} ∩ A\right)$ which $ϕ$ always,

Now checking symmetric we will interchange $A \text{ and } B$,

So, $\left(B ∩ {A}^{c}\right) ∪ \left({B}^{c} ∩ A\right)$ which is same as $\left(A ∩ {B}^{c}\right) ∪ \left({A}^{c} ∩ B\right)$, hence the relation is symmetric,

So, ${R}_{1}$ is reflexive, symmetric

Now checking for transitive
$\left(A ∩ {B}^{c}\right) ∪ \left({A}^{c} ∩ B\right) = ϕ;$

Now from diagram the elements in $\left(A ∩ {B}^{c}\right) ∪ \left({A}^{c} ∩ B\right)$ will be,

$\left\{a\right\} ∪ \left\{b\right\}$ which is given as empty set $ϕ$

Hence, we can say that, $\left\{a\right\} = ϕ = \left\{b\right\} ⇒ A = B$

Now taking, $( B ∩ {C}^{c} ) ∪ ( {B}^{c} ∩ C ) = ϕ ∴ B = C$

$∴ A = C$ equivalence.

Now solving,

${R}_{2} ≡ A ∪ {B}^{c} = {A}^{c} ∪ B$

Now for reflexive replacing $B \to A$ we get,

$A ∪ {A}^{c} = {A}^{c} ∪ A$ which is true,

And for symmetric interchanging $A ⇔ B$ we get,

$B ∪ {A}^{c} = {B}^{c} ∪ A$ which is again true,

Hence, ${R}_{2} \to$ Reflexive, symmetric

Now for transitive,

From diagram the elements in$A ∪ {B}^{c} = {A}^{c} ∪ B ⇒ \left\{a, c, d\right\} = \left\{b, c, d\right\}$

On comparing both side, we get $\left\{a\right\} = \left\{b\right\} ∴ A = B$

And, $B ∪ {C}^{c} = {B}^{c} ∪ C ⇒ B = C$

$∴ A = C ∴ A ∪ {C}^{c} = {A}^{c} ∪ C$

$∴$ Equivalence

Hence, both given relation are equivalence.

questions.q: Let $R$ be a relation defined on $\mathbb{N}$ as a $R$ b is $2a + 3b$ is a multiple of $5, a, b \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $R$ is
questions.solution:
Given:

$R = \left\{\left(a, b\right): 2a + 3bisdivisibleby5fora, b \in N\right\}$

Reflexive:

$2a + 3a = 5a$ is always divisible by $5$.

So, $\left(a, a\right) \in R$

Symmetric:

Let $\left(a, b\right) \in R$ i.e., $2a + 3b = 5\lambda$, where $\lambda \in {Z}^{+}$.

Now,

$5a + 5b = multipleof5$

$⇒ \left(2a + 3b\right) + \left(2b + 3a\right) = multipleof5$

$⇒ 5\lambda + \left(2b + 3a\right) = multipleof5$

$⇒ 2b + 3a = multipleof5 - 5\lambda$

So, $2b + 3a$ is divisible by $5$

Transitive:

Let $\left(a, b\right), \left(b, c\right) \in R$, then

$2a + 3b = 5{\lambda}_{1}; {\lambda}_{1} \in {Z}^{+}$

$2b + 3c = 5{\lambda}_{2}; {\lambda}_{2} \in {Z}^{+}$

So,

$2a + 5b + 3c = 5\left({\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ 2a + 3c = 5\left({\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2} - b\right)$

Hence, $2a + 3c$ is divisible by $5$, so $\left(a, c\right) \in R$

Hence, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

It is symmetric.

Transitive:

$\left(a, b\right)R\left(c, d\right) ⇒ \dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{1}{b} = \dfrac{1}{d} - \dfrac{1}{c}$

$\left(c, d\right)R\left(e, f\right) = \dfrac{1}{c} - \dfrac{1}{d} = \dfrac{1}{e} - \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{1}{b} = \dfrac{1}{e} - \dfrac{1}{f}$

$⇒ \left(a, b\right) R \left(e, f\right)$

So, not transitive.

questions.q: In a group of $100$ persons $75$ speak English and $40$ speak Hindi. Each person speaks at least one of the two languages. If the number of persons who speak only English is $\alpha$ and the number of persons who speaks only Hindi is $\beta$, then the eccentricity of the ellipse $25\left({\beta}^{2}{x}^{2} + {\alpha}^{2}{y}^{2}\right) = {\alpha}^{2}{\beta}^{2}$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

In a group of $100$ persons $75$ speak English and $40$ speak Hindi,

And each person speaks at least one of the two languages,

And the number of persons who speak only English is $\alpha$ and the number of persons who speaks only Hindi is $\beta$,

Now from above diagram we can see that,

$\beta = 100 - 75 = 25$

So, $\alpha = 75 - \left(40 - 25\right) = 60$

Hence, number of people who speak English only is $\alpha = 60$ and Hindi is $\beta = 25$,

Now putting the value in given equation of ellipse we get,

$25\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{60}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{25}^{2}}\right] = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{36 \times 4} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{25} = 1$

Now comparing with $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ we get, $a = 12 \text{ and } b = 5$

Now we know that,

Eccentricity of ellipse is given by $e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}$

$⇒ e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{25}{36 \times 4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{119}}{12}$
